arxiv-1705-09213.title: Graphical Methods in Device-Independent Quantum Cryptography
arxiv-1705-09213.creator: Spencer Breiner, 1 Carl A. Miller, 1,2 and Neil J. Ross 2,3 1 National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Gaithersburg, MD 20899, USA 2 Joint Center for Quantum Information and Computer Science (QuICS) University of Maryland, College Park, MD 20742, USA 3 Department of Mathematics and Stat
arxiv-1705-09213.description: Abstract We introduce a framework for graphical security proofs in device-independent quantum cryptography using the methods of categorical quantum mechanics. We are optimistic that this approach will make some of the highly complex proofs in quantum cryptography more accessible, facilitate the discovery of new proofs, and enable automated proof verification.

arxiv-2101-04143.title: Diagonal Sums of Doubly Stochastic Matrices Department of Mathematics, University of Oslo, Norway. geird@math.uio.no. Corresponding author.
arxiv-2101-04143.creator: Richard A. Brualdi
arxiv-2101-04143.description: Abstract Let Ω n \Omega_{n} denote the class of n × n n\times n doubly stochastic matrices (each such matrix is entrywise nonnegative and every row and column sum is 1). We study the diagonals of matrices in Ω n \Omega_{n} .

arxiv-2204-01296.title: Technology and jobs: A systematic literature review
arxiv-2204-01296.creator: Kerstin Hötte 1,2 , Melline Somers 3 , Angelos Theodorakopoulos 1 1 Oxford Martin School, University of Oxford, 34 Broad Street, Oxford OX1 3BD, UK 2 Institute for New Economic Thinking, University of Oxford, Manor Road, Oxford OX1 3UQ, UK 3 Research Centre for Education and the Labour Market, Maast
arxiv-2204-01296.description: Abstract Does technological change destroy or create jobs? New technologies may replace human workers, but can simultaneously create jobs if workers are needed to use these technologies or if new economic activities emerge. Furthermore, technology-driven productivity growth may increase disposable income, stimulating a demand-induced expansion of employment.

arxiv-2210-00634.title: A Kernel Measure of Dissimilarity between M M Distributions Thanks: Supported by NSF grant DMS-2015376
arxiv-2210-00634.creator: Zhen Huang
arxiv-2210-00634.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Zhen Huang. Given M ≥ 2 M\geq 2 distributions defined on a general measurable space, we introduce a nonparametric (kernel) measure of multi-sample dissimilarity (KMD) — a parameter that quantifies the difference between the M M distributions. The population KMD, which takes values between 0 and 1, is 0 if and only if all the M M distributions are the same, and 1 if and only if all the distributions are mutually singular.

arxiv-2307-05265.title: Computing minimal distinguishing Hennessy-Milner formulas is NP-hard, but variants are tractable
arxiv-2307-05265.creator: Jan Martens, Jan Friso Groote
arxiv-2307-05265.description: Abstract We study the problem of computing minimal distinguishing formulas for non-bisimilar states in finite LTSs. We show that this is NP-hard if the size of the formula must be minimal. Similarly, the existence of a short distinguishing trace is NP-complete.

arxiv-2309-08620.title: Variance Reduction of Resampling for Sequential Monte Carlo
arxiv-2309-08620.creator: Xiongming Dai, Gerald Baumgartner
arxiv-2309-08620.description: Abstract A resampling scheme provides a way to switch low-weight particles for sequential Monte Carlo with higher-weight particles representing the objective distribution. The less the variance of the weight distribution is, the more concentrated the effective particles are, and the quicker and more accurate it is to approximate the hidden Markov model, especially for the nonlinear case.

arxiv-2310-19291.title: A3SA: Advanced Data Augmentation via Adjoint Sensitivity Analysis
arxiv-2310-19291.creator: Chanik Kang†, Dongjin Seo†, Svetlana V. Boriskina, Haejun Chung*
arxiv-2310-19291.description: Abstract Innovative machine learning techniques have facilitated the inverse design of photonic structures for numerous practical applications. Nevertheless, within these approaches, the quantity of data and the initial data distribution are paramount for the discovery of highly efficient photonic devices. These devices often require simulated data ranging from thousands to several hundred thousand data points.

arxiv-2406-16274.title: Dynamical structures of misaligned circumbinary planets under hierarchical three-body systems
arxiv-2406-16274.creator: Hanlun Lei, Yan-Xiang Gong
arxiv-2406-16274.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Hanlun Lei, Yan-Xiang Gong. All circumbinary planets (CBPs) currently detected are located in almost co-planar configurations with respect to the binary orbit, due to the fact that CBPs with higher misalignment are more difficult to detect. However, observations of polar circumbinary gas and debris disks in recent years and long-term orbital stability of inclined planets indicate that it is possible to form misaligned CBPs around eccentricity binaries (even polar CBPs).

arxiv-2412-10796.title: Spatio-temporal analysis of extreme winter temperatures in Ireland
arxiv-2412-10796.creator: Dáire Healy, Jonathan A. Tawn, Peter Thorne, Andrew Parnell
arxiv-2412-10796.description: Abstract We analyse synoptic observational data on extreme daily minimum temperatures in winter months over Ireland from 1950–2022. We model the tail of the marginal distributions of extreme winter minima using a generalised Pareto distribution capturing temporal and spatial sources of non-stationarity. We disentangle long-term climate trends from obfuscating shorter-term (month-to-winter long) large fluctuations, caused by e.g.

arxiv-2505-18003.title: An Example Safety Case for Safeguards Against Misuse
arxiv-2505-18003.creator: Joshua Clymer †, Jonah Weinbaum ‡*, Robert Kirk §*, Kimberly Mai §, Selena Zhang ⋄, Xander Davies §, † Redwood Research, ‡ MATS, ⋄ MIT, § UK AI Security Institute
arxiv-2505-18003.description: Abstract Existing evaluations of AI misuse safeguards provide a patchwork of evidence that is often difficult to connect to real-world decisions. To bridge this gap, we describe an end-to-end argument (a “safety case”) that misuse safeguards reduce the risk posed by an AI assistant to low levels.

pmc-10638630.title: The Price of Explainability in Machine Learning Models for 100-Day Readmission Prediction in Heart Failure: Retrospective, Comparative, Machine Learning Study
pmc-10638630.creator: Amira Soliman, Björn Agvall, Kobra Etminani, Omar Hamed, Markus Lingman, Amaryllis Mavragani, Gilbert Lim, Yonglai Zhang
pmc-10638630.description: BackgroundSensitive and interpretable machine learning (ML) models can provide valuable assistance to clinicians in managing patients with heart failure (HF) at discharge by identifying individual factors associated with a high risk of readmission. In this cohort study, we delve into the factors driving the potential utility of classification models as decision support tools for predicting readmissions in patients with HF.

pmc-11332300.title: Defining military sexual trauma: establishing parameters and perspectives
pmc-11332300.creator: Charlotte Herriott, Gavin Campbell, Lauren Godier-McBard, Abigail Wood, Dominic Murphy
pmc-11332300.description: Background: The term military sexual trauma [MST] is increasingly used to describe instances of sexual harassment/assault that occur between serving personnel during military service. However, in the absence of a clear universal definition, MST is an increasingly contested term, with confusion about its scope, application to differing jurisdictions and implications for responses and treatment.

pmc-11390340.title: Hdac3 deficiency limits periosteal reaction associated with Western diet feeding in female mice
pmc-11390340.creator: Elizabeth K. Vu, Ismael Y. Karkache, Anthony Pham, Jinsha Koroth, Elizabeth W. Bradley
pmc-11390340.description: Diet‐induced obesity is associated with enhanced systemic inflammation that limits bone regeneration. HDAC inhibitors are currently being explored as anti‐inflammatory agents. Prior reports show that myeloid progenitor‐directed Hdac3 ablation enhances intramembranous bone healing in female mice. In this study, we determined if Hdac3 ablation increased intramembranous bone regeneration in mice fed a high‐fat/high‐sugar (HFD) diet.

pmc-11406438.title: Dioscin protects against chronic prostatitis through the TLR4/NF-κB pathway
pmc-11406438.creator: Yan Long, Xiaodong Ge, Liangliang Ma, Junhua Guo, Yong Zhu
pmc-11406438.description: This study aimed to elucidate the effects and potential mechanisms of dioscin on chronic prostatitis (CP) in vivo and in vitro. CP models were constructed in vivo and in vitro and treated with different concentrations of dioscin. Hematoxylin and eosin staining was used to investigate the morphology of the prostate tissues.

pmc-11631737.title: Emerging roles of mechanosensitive ion channels in ventilator induced lung injury: a systematic review
pmc-11631737.creator: Gang Liu, Bin-bin Dong, Shalika Devanarayana, Rong-Chang Chen, Qi Liu
pmc-11631737.description: BackgroundThe pathogenetic mechanisms of ventilator-induced lung injury (VILI) still need to be elucidated. The mechanical forces during mechanical ventilation are continually sensed and transmitted by mechanosensitive ion channels (MSICs) in pulmonary endothelial, epithelial, and immune cells. In recent years, MSICs have been shown to be involved in VILI.

pmc-12700386.title: Investigation of the effect and mechanisms of moxa smoke in the treatment of Influenza A Virus (IAV) infection

pmc-12700386.description: Influenza, primarily caused by the Influenza A virus, is a highly contagious respiratory disease. While moxa burning is a traditional method used to reduce respiratory infections, most studies have focused on the components of moxa and air disinfection, often neglecting the pharmacological effects and mechanisms of moxa smoke.

pmc-13110487.title: Growth performance and physiometabolic safety of probiotic–Curcuma herbal supplementation in local female lambs of Indonesia
pmc-13110487.creator: Yanuartono Yanuartono, Alfarisa Nururrozi, Soedarmanto Indarjulianto, Alsi Dara Paryuni, Dwi Sunu Datrianto, Imron Rosyadi, Hary Purnamaningsih
pmc-13110487.description: Background and Aim:The escalating demand for animal protein in Indonesia underscores the imperative for efficacious nutritional strategies to augment lamb productivity while safeguarding physiological integrity. Prior investigations have predominantly examined probiotics or herbal additives in isolation, yielding fragmented insights into their combined efficacy.

pmc-13201376.title: Towards a Unified Research Agenda: International Consensus to Advance Understanding and Prevention of Sudden Unexpected Death in Epilepsy
pmc-13201376.creator: Hannah Pickard, Elaine K. O’Loughlin, Mary Holmay, Gardiner Lapham, Jeffrey Buchhalter, Ben Donovan, Amol Bhandare, Rob C. Wykes, Arjune Sen, Laura S. Lubbers
pmc-13201376.description: Sudden unexpected death in epilepsy (SUDEP) is a significant research and community priority. uslaw-usc-t50-s4305.description: United States Code, Title 50 (War And National Defense); Chapter 53 (Trading With The Enemy). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) The President, if he shall find it compatible with the safety of the United States and with the successful prosecution of the war, may, by proclamation, suspend the provisions of this chapter so far as they apply to an ally of.

uslaw-usc-t52-s30126.title: 52 U.S.C. § 30126 — Prohibition of contributions by minors
uslaw-usc-t52-s30126.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t52-s30126.description: United States Code, Title 52 (Voting And Elections); Chapter 301 (Federal Election Campaigns); Subchapter I (Disclosure Of Federal Campaign Funds). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. An individual who is 17 years old or younger shall not make a contribution to a candidate or a contribution or donation to a committee of a political party.
